title: Noailles (Venice) to the Cardinal de Lorraine, 13 Nov 1558: BnF fr. 3151 no. 33

plaintext.source: The court's decipherment written beside each cipher block in the inner margin; the start of each gloss line is lost in the binding.

transcription.notes: Not transcribed: two cipher blocks of three lines on f. 60r, about 150 signs (estimate from NOTES).

system.summary: A symbol cipher different from La Guiche's, two blocks of about 150 signs in all; not analysed.
system.notes: Split from guiche1551 on 14 Oct 2026; a different symbol alphabet from La Guiche (1551).

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherment in the inner margin of f. 60r, partly lost in the gutter.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5 and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Downloaded the Gallica volume fr. 3151 and located item 33 (views 60-61).

Found the court's decipherment in the inner margin beside each of the two cipher blocks on f. 60r; the binding hides the start of each gloss line ('... mauluaise ... gouvernement ... affaires'; '... grand seigneur ... ne luy ... de la fortune ...').

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): catalogue item 10 had grouped three letters in three different ciphers. La Guiche's 22-sign substitution stays in guiche1551; Noailles's Venice letter (another symbol alphabet) went to noailles1558 and Seure's six Lisbon letters (homophonic with numeral codes) to seure1558. The Noailles cipher itself was not transcribed or attacked.

outcome.method_basis: A contemporary marginal decipherment exists but is cut by the binding; the cipher (about 150 signs) was neither transcribed nor attacked here, so no text was obtained.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Nothing transcribed or deciphered; the legible gloss words are not counted.
